test.title: Should children be paid for chores?
textTitles: Should children be paid for chores?

texts.title: Should children be paid for chores?

paragraphs.text: Paying children for household jobs is common, and many parents defend it as a way to teach the value of money. I understand the reasoning, but I think it sends the wrong message about what it means to be part of a family.

Some tasks, such as keeping one’s own room tidy or clearing the table after dinner, are simply what everyone in a household does. If children are paid for these, they may reasonably ask why they should help at all when they do not need the money.

That said, I see nothing wrong with paying for jobs that go beyond normal family duties, such as washing the car or helping a neighbour with their garden. These can teach children that effort can be exchanged for income.

Pocket money can also be given without any link to chores. A regular weekly amount allows children to practise saving and making choices, and in my experience it is at least as effective at teaching the value of money.
